denial.label: Pre-existing disease waiting period not completed

grounds: Chronic kidney disease stage 3 was first diagnosed on 2025-03-17, AFTER the policy start date 2023-07-22; by definition it is not a Pre-Existing Disease, so the waiting period does not apply.
letter:
Subject: Appeal against Denial D03 – Claim ID 2c588417-7537-a68c-96f4-d0aab903812f

Claim Details:  
Patient Name: Cristin Na Jast (Patient ID: 2c588417-7537-a68c-7c2d-e1a45847fcc9)  
Date of Service: 2025-03-17  
Procedure: Alcohol Use Disorder Identification Test – Consumption (AUDIT‑C)  
Total Claim Amount: INR 11,921.24  
Plan: Suraksha Silver Individual Health Plan (Plan Code: SGH‑SILVER)  
Insurer: Suraksha General Health Insurance Ltd.

Grounds for Appeal – Pre‑Existing Disease Definition:  
The diagnosis of Chronic Kidney Disease stage 3 was made on 2025‑03‑17, which is after the policy start date of 2023‑07‑22. According to Clause 2.2, a condition first diagnosed on or after the policy start date is not a Pre‑Existing Disease, irrespective of its chronic nature [suraksha_silver_policy#5].

Grounds for Appeal – Waiting Period Applicability:  
Clause 4.2 states that the Pre‑Existing Disease waiting period applies only to conditions that satisfy the definition in Clause 2.2. Because the CKD diagnosis does not meet that definition, the 36‑month waiting period is inapplicable and the claim should be covered without restriction [suraksha_silver_policy#11].

Clinical Necessity:  
The treating physician has determined that the AUDIT‑C screening is essential for the comprehensive management of the patient’s Chronic Kidney Disease stage 3, as it evaluates alcohol consumption that can affect renal function. The physician will attach detailed clinical notes to substantiate the medical necessity of this test.

Reference to Denial Standards – Burden of Proof:  
Under the insurer’s own denial standards, the burden of proving that an exclusion or waiting period applies rests with the insurer. For a Pre‑Existing Disease denial, the insurer must provide documentary evidence that the condition was diagnosed before the policy start date, which has not been presented in this case [claims_procedure_and_grievance#6].

Specific Request:  
In view of the foregoing, we respectfully request that the denial be withdrawn, the claim be reprocessed, and the amount of INR 11,921.24 be paid in full in accordance with the policy terms.

Insurance Desk (on behalf of the treating provider)

citations.section: Suraksha Silver Individual Health Plan (Policy Wording) > 4. Waiting Periods > 4.2 Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Period
citations.quote:
### 4.2 Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Period
Expenses related to a Pre-Existing Disease (as defined in Clause 2.2) are covered only after 36 months of continuous coverage from the first policy start date. This waiting period applies ONLY to conditions meeting the definition in Clause 2.2.

citations.section: Claims Procedure, Denial Standards and Grievance Redressal > C3. Standards for Denial > C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
citations.quote:
### C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
The insurer bears the burden of proving that an exclusion or waiting period applies. For a Pre-Existing Disease denial, the insurer must show documentary evidence that the condition was diagnosed or treated before the policy start date.
